findings.title: Floats inside new flex container are ignored in .small-action
findings.body: `.small-action` now uses `@include flexbox()`, which makes its children flex items. `float` has no effect on flex items, so `.topic-avatar { float: left }` (line 270) and `button { float: right }` (line 309) no longer position as before — the button will no longer be right-aligned. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button (and remove the floats) to preserve the layout.

findings.title: Header panel loses right alignment without flexbox support
findings.body: `.panel`'s `float: right` was replaced by `margin-left: auto` + `@include order(3)`, which only work when the parent is a flex container. In browsers that don't support modern flexbox (where the `display: flex` fallbacks in the mixin resolve to the legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` models that ignore `margin: auto`), the panel will be rendered left-aligned in normal flow, breaking the header. Also `.icons`/`.login-button` still use `float: left`, which is ignored on flex items, so those rules are now dead.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for flex-* keywords
findings.body: The mixin blindly forwards `$alignment` to legacy properties. `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` do not accept the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end` keywords (they expect `start`/`end`), so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently emit invalid declarations in the legacy prefixes while looking correct. Map values explicitly or drop the obsolete `-webkit-box-align`/`-ms-flex-align` lines.

findings.title: order mixin mixes 0-based and 1-based ordinal values
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1) while the standard `order` is 0-based (default 0). Passing the same `$val` to both means legacy box-model browsers compute a different relative ordering than standard-flexbox browsers (e.g. `order(2)` is one step from default in old syntax vs two in new). Either emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group properties or drop them.

findings.title: inline-flex fallback ordering can override the better prefix
findings.body: In `inline-flex()`, `-moz-inline-box` is declared after `-webkit-inline-flex`. If a UA understood both (and generally for cascade correctness), the older legacy value wins because it comes last. Legacy/box-model fallbacks should be listed before the newer prefixed and standard values, as done in `flexbox()`.
